statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-107822 (GHSA-2m85-2x26-36rf, MDEV-40541): from MariaDB 10.6.1 until 11.8.9 and the other fixed releases, the server's ACL cache built the same database-privilege cache key for a role and for a user@localhost account with the same name, because both used an empty IP component, so an attacker with CREATE USER could create the colliding account and, once the other principal's privileges were cached, use the database privileges granted to it. It is fixed in MariaDB 11.8.9 by upstream commit 67ea07dd3400004e4f7ae01bf977f4344bbe064b, which changes acl_get in sql/sql_acl.cc: https://github.com/MariaDB/server/security/advisories/GHSA-2m85-2x26-36rf, https://github.com/MariaDB/server/commit/67ea07dd3400004e4f7ae01bf977f4344bbe064b, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-107822. The DHI mariadb packages backport that change onto 11.8.6 from the fourth DHI rebuild, the version this range names as fixed. We checked every mariadb build published in the DHI Debian repository: four successive DHI rebuilds of Debian's mariadb 1:11.8.6-0+deb13u1 (called the first to fourth rebuild below; the fourth is the current build), each with 56 binary packages per architecture including the -dbgsym packages, on amd64 and arm64; every package read was verified against the repository index checksum. Between the third and fourth rebuilds the server binary's acl_get function changes size on both architectures (from the -dbgsym symbol tables), the MDEV-40541 regression test is in mysql-test/main/grant5.result of mariadb-test-data in the fourth rebuild and absent in the first three, and the Debian changelog shipped in mariadb-server-core records the backport in the fourth rebuild only. The range ends at the first build that carries it.
